author: Shri Raghavendra Swami
commentary: किञ्च क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः अकार्येच्छा, परवित्तापहरणाद्यधर्मे धर्मबुद्धिरित्यादि मिथ्याज्ञानं वा । संमोहादुक्तद्विरूपात् स्मृतिविभ्रमः क्रमात्प्रतिषेधादिस्मृतिनाशः, परवित्तापहरणादेरधर्मत्वाद्यभिधायकश्रुत्याद्यर्थस्य पूर्वं स्वयं ज्ञातस्याप्यन्यथा स्मरणं वा । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशः येन पूर्वं निर्णीतदोषबुद्धेः सर्वात्मना नाशो भवति । तन्नाशात् तेन चाधर्मकरणाच्च प्रणश्यति नरकाद्यनर्थं प्राप्नोति । एतदुक्तं भवति, रागद्वेषयोः परम्परया नरकाद्यनर्थप्राप्तिः फलमिति ज्ञानेन तत्परिजिहीर्षायां, विषयध्यानं परम्परया तत्कारणमिति ज्ञानेन तदकरणाद्रागद्वेषयोरनुत्पाद इति ॥ २.६३॥
translation:
From anger results the wrong wish; from (this) wrong wish, forgetfulness (of Law); from (this) forgetfulness, loss of judgement; from the loss of judgement, he perishes. (63) 
V. When the accomplishment of a desire is checked by anything, anger bursts forth. Sammoha or the wrong wish is the inclination to do what ought not to be done: it may be mistaking the unrighteous conduct of appropriating another's wealth, &c, to be perfectly righteous. Front such a wrong tendency and such unrighteous activities the memory of Laws prohibiting them becomes impaired and the very sacred rules once so clearly understood by himself may now give him a very different meaning, why, they may seem to sanction to his wrong ways. Then gradually comes the loss of judgement which allows him unrestrained to be more and more wicked things. When he is thus concentrated in evil, He must purely go to hell and suffer the consequences. The significance of this genesis of passions, especially of Likes and Dislikes is: When it is known that they lead, stop by step, to hell and other sufferings, there comes the wish to get rid of them; he first ceases to muse on the objects of senses and then gradually checks the growth of those passions and eventually destroys their root. :(62 & 63.) 
A. Like and Dislike may go, os has been shown above. But what effect does that leave behind? It is the control of the senses, the Lord says; He also gives the effect of this control in the following.
